claim: For every integer \(m\ge 4\), let \(\Theta_m\) be the graph with two vertices joined by \(m\) parallel edges, let \(B_3(\Theta_m)\) be the unordered configuration space of three points, and let \(A_m=\ker(\mathbb Z^m\xrightarrow{\sum}\mathbb Z)\) be the edge augmentation lattice. Permuting edges gives \(S_m\)-actions, and \(H_2(B_3(\Theta_m);\mathbb Z)\cong\bigwedge^3 A_m\) equivariantly. Under a consistent orientation, the theta class on ordered distinct edges \(i,j,k,l\) maps to \((e_j-e_i)\wedge(e_k-e_i)\wedge(e_l-e_i)\). Hence the theta classes containing any fixed edge form an integral basis, and all integral relations among oriented four-edge theta classes are generated by the five-term boundary relations on five distinct edges.
integrity: The infinite-family proof is algebraic, using the reduced Świątkowski complex, the vertex-explosion exact sequence, and exactness of the Koszul complex. The included finite verifier checks the theta-coordinate and relation matrices for \(4\le m\le10\) over several finite fields but is not used as a substitute for the unbounded proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is for unordered three-point configuration spaces of generalized theta graphs in homological degree \(2\). No claim is made for higher particle number, higher homological degree, ordered configurations, or cohomology products. The orientation of an individual theta generator is conventional, although the module and relation lattice are intrinsic.
title: Complete theta-class relations for three-point generalized theta configurations
